newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market stalled - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market stalled - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday on Wednesday were inactive, with cattle owners and packers in a standoff, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids at $64.00 per cwt were steady with limited sales on Tuesday but were passed by owners pricing cattle from $65.00 to $66.00, sources said.
Active sales in Nebraska Tuesday at higher prices encouraged owners in Kansas and the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area to resist bids at $64.00, cattle feeders said.
About 80,000 head sold Tuesday in Nebraska mostly $1.00 higher at $106.00 per cwt on a dressed basis and $65.00/live. Thin sales were also reported at $65.50-$66.50, sources and USDA said.
Nebraska's hefty one-day sales near 80,000 head were close to the record high set earlier this year on April 30 of 94,400, USDA statistics showed.

Fed cattle prices this week were underpinned by steep advances in beef values amid tight stocks and moderate retail demand. Retailer buying ranged from fill-in buying to replace beef sold last weekend to last-minute inventory building for planned beef advertising promotions at the end of the month and for the Independence Day holiday, sources said.
Fed cattle prices also were seen buoyed by the ability of feedlots to remain current in their marketings, they said.
